chunks: and struggle against Satan so he does not take the reins of your affairs,
and turn your face towards the Hereafter,
for it is our path and your path.
and beware lest Allah strike you with a sudden affliction from him that touches the root and cuts off the branches,
for I swear to you by Allah an oath that is not broken,
if destiny brings me and you together,
"Until Allah judges between us, and He is the Best of the judges."

key_terms.قَارِعَةٍ: a sudden affliction or striking calamity
key_terms.قِيَادَكَ: your reins/leashes (metaphor for control or guidance)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'touching the root and cutting the branches' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This letter, addressed to Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, serves as a pivotal political and spiritual exhortation where Ali (AS) contrasts his own steadfastness with Mu'awiya's ambition, urging him to prioritize the Hereafter over worldly power. The warning of a 'sudden affliction' (qari'ah) touching the 'root' (asl) and 'branches' (dabir) reflects the Shia view of divine retribution against usurpers, while the concluding oath underscores the ultimate authority of Allah as the best judge in the conflict between truth and falsehood.

en.sayed-ali-raza: You should fear Allāh about yourself
and not allow Satan to lead you.
Turn your face towards the next world
because that is our path and your path,
and fear that Allāh may not entangle you in any sudden infliction which may destroy the root as well as cut away the branches.
I swear to you by Allāh an oath which will not be broken
that if destiny brings me and you together
I shall steadfastly hold before you: Until Allāh judges between us, and He is the Best of the judges. (Qur’ān, 7:87)
